newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia dealers see T-bill yield rise at Sept 25 sa.
newsitem.headline: Russia dealers see T-bill yield rise at Sept 25 sa.

text.p: Russia's finance ministry will have to raise Treasury bill yields at Wednesday's auctions as there will be little demand from Russian and Western investors unnerved by President Boris Yeltsin's health problems, dealers said on Tuesday.
The finance ministry will offer four trillion roubles in four-month T-bills and seven trillion roubles in six-month paper at auctions on Wednesday.
The top surgeon likely to perform a heart operation on Yeltsin said on Sunday that it might be delayed for up to two months for the operation, or call it off altogether.
On Tuesday he said the operation could not be cancelled.
"After the Yeltsin news we are not expecting much participation from non-residents," said Dmitry Shepelev from Alfa-Bank.
Yeltsin's spokesman said on Tuesday that doctors, including U.S. surgeon Michael DeBakey would meet on Wednesday to discuss a possible date for the operation.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said there could be no talk of Yeltsin's resignation over health problems as proposed by communists.
Dealers forecast yields would rise in the range of between 75 and 85 percent, compared with 61.25 percent at the previous auction of six-month paper on September 18.
They said the rise would also be spurred by the actions of the finance ministry, in particular its sale of about one trillion roubles worth of T-bills on a falling market in the last two days.
"Today's trading finished lamentably (for the finance ministry)," said Konstantin Demchenko from Natsionalny Reservny Bank. "It is clear the finance ministry needs funds to pay the Maritime Region."
Many workers in the Far Eastern Maritime region have been on a hunger strike for about two weeks, demanding several months back pay.
